title: Low-latency span queue and compact metric surface refactor
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Reduce runtime telemetry overhead by replacing sync exporters and high-cardinality metric encodings with an async, low-allocation span queue and a compact metric surface for the serving runtime.
description: Background: the serving runtime and sidecar instrumentation currently incur measurable CPU and latency overhead due to synchronous OTEL exporters, frequent allocations for span envelopes, and wide metric labels. That overhead shows up as higher p99 tail latency on short requests and elevated CPU usage during peak traffic. This ticket implements a lower-latency span queue (lock-free ring buffer with bounded batching), a compact metric surface to reduce label cardinality and serialization size, and a collectorless bridge mode to decouple runtime from full OTEL Collector dependencies. Outcomes: reduce instrumentation p99 overhead, lower CPU by ~20-30% on hot paths, and shrink telemetry network egress by ~40% for busy tenants.
technical_notes: Introduce a ring-buffer span queue that accepts completed spans from hotpaths and hands off to a background worker for batching and protobuf encoding.
Replace per-span JSON envelope allocations with preallocated protobuf buffers and an arena-like allocator to avoid GC spikes.
Add a compact metric surface layer: map common label sets to stable integer tags, emit histogram buckets with compressed encoding, and prune low-importance labels via a config-driven prefilter.

Implement collectorless bridge: format spans/metrics in a lightweight capnp/protobuf envelope compatible with our telemetry gateway so we can remove direct dependency on the full OTEL collector in the runtime.
Upgrade OTel SDK to 1.18 (or latest LTS) and move to the SDK's async exporter hooks; keep compatibility shim for older collector endpoints.
Expose runtime flags to control sampling, batch sizes, and queue depth for canary tuning (defaults tuned for latency-critical tenants).
Keep a compatibility mode that can fall back to the legacy synchronous exporter upon OOM or queue saturation.
Profiling: add temporary flamegraph endpoints and an e2e benchmark harness to compare before/after perf on representative traces (seq len distribution, tokenization load).
acceptance_criteria: Per-request instrumentation p99 added latency reduced from baseline (measured) by >=50% on small requests (<128 tokens).
CPU usage of runtime process under identical load reduced by >=20% in our staging cluster benchmarks.
Telemetry egress (bytes/min) reduced by >=30% for the top 10 tenants due to compact metric encoding and label pruning.
No loss of critical spans: sampling shims must preserve 100% of traced error spans and 95% of canary-sampled traces during rollout.
Can be toggled on/off via runtime config without requiring binary rollbacks.
Automated integration tests covering queue saturation, exporter failover, and compatibility with existing downstream telemetry pipeline.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Feature flagged implementation in runtime: land code behind 'compact_telemetry_v2' and 'span_queue' flags.
Phase 1 - Internal canary: enable for 5% of internal traffic, compare telemetry metrics and application latency over 48h.
Phase 2 - Customer alpha: enable for two low-risk tenants with high token throughput; monitor for 7 days.
Phase 3 - Ramp to 25% and tune batch size / queue depth using staging workload replay.
Phase 4 - Full rollout for latency-critical fleets, keep legacy exporter enabled in fallback mode for 30 days before removal.
Rollback criteria: increase in error traces, >5% regressions in p99 application latency, or unexpected telemetry loss.
risks: Queue saturation could delay delivery of spans during sudden traffic spikes; mitigated by bounded queue + backpressure and drop-policy for non-critical spans.
Incorrect label pruning could remove customer-facing metric dimensions; mitigate via staged config and per-tenant allowlists.
Protobuf/compact envelope bugs could break downstream processors; address with compatibility tests and a translation shim in the telemetry gateway.
Upgrading OTEL SDK may change semantic defaults (attribute renaming, samplers) — include interop tests and run both SDKs in shadow mode during migration.
Memory churn from arena allocator if not tuned; include leak hunting and OOM guards in the implementation.
test_plan: Unit tests for ring buffer correctness under concurrent producers and single consumer.
Integration tests for exporter failover: simulate network errors and assert fallback to legacy exporter and eventual delivery.
Load tests: run k6-style replay of production traffic in staging to validate p99 latency and CPU improvements.
Compatibility suite: end-to-end check with telemetry gateway to ensure compact envelopes are decoded properly and metrics reorder correctly.
Chaos test: kill background export worker and ensure the runtime continues serving and recovers without panics.
